title: SQL Basics: Quick Revision Notes
summary: End-to-end revision of relational SQL: defining tables with types and keys, changing and querying rows, joining tables, aggregating with GROUP BY, and handling NULL correctly.

chapters.title: SQL Mental Model and Tables
points: Relational model: a table is rows (records) by typed columns, and SQL is declarative: you state the result you want, the engine picks the plan
CREATE TABLE users (id INT PRIMARY KEY, email VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL UNIQUE, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);
Core types: INT/BIGINT, DECIMAL(p,s) for exact money, FLOAT for approximate, VARCHAR(n)/TEXT, BOOLEAN, DATE, TIMESTAMP
Constraints: NOT NULL, UNIQUE, DEFAULT, CHECK (price > 0), PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY
Statement families: DDL defines structure (CREATE, ALTER, DROP), DML changes and reads data (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT)

chapters.title: Primary and Foreign Keys
points: Primary key = unique + NOT NULL row identifier; one per table, may be composite PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id)
Foreign key: a column whose values must exist in the referenced table's key: customer_id INT REFERENCES customers(id)
Referential actions: ON DELETE CASCADE removes child rows, SET NULL clears the reference, RESTRICT/NO ACTION blocks the delete
Surrogate key (auto-increment id) vs natural key (email, ISBN): natural keys change, so prefer a surrogate PK plus a UNIQUE constraint
Insert order: parent rows first, delete order: children first, or the foreign key rejects the statement; FK columns are not auto-indexed in most engines, so index them yourself

chapters.title: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and SELECT
points: INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ('a@x.com','Asha'), ('b@x.com','Bo'); always list columns so schema changes do not break it
UPDATE orders SET status = 'shipped' WHERE id = 7; DELETE FROM orders WHERE id = 7; omit WHERE and every row changes
SELECT col1, col2 FROM t WHERE cond ORDER BY col DESC LIMIT 10; avoid SELECT * in production code
Logical execution order: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT, so a SELECT alias works in ORDER BY but not in WHERE
WHERE operators: = <> < >, AND/OR/NOT, IN (1,2), BETWEEN a AND b (inclusive), LIKE 'A%' (% any run, _ one char); AND binds tighter than OR, so use parentheses

chapters.title: Joins
points: INNER JOIN returns only rows with a match on both sides: FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN keeps every left row and fills right columns with NULL when unmatched; RIGHT JOIN is the mirror; FULL OUTER keeps both sides' unmatched rows
Anti-join pattern: LEFT JOIN ... WHERE right.id IS NULL finds left rows with no match (customers with no orders)
Filtering the right table in WHERE turns a LEFT JOIN into an inner join; put that condition in the ON clause instead
Missing or wrong ON condition produces a CROSS JOIN (rows multiply to m x n); a one-to-many join duplicates the parent row once per child

chapters.title: GROUP BY, HAVING and NULL Semantics
points: GROUP BY collapses rows into groups; aggregates COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX run per group: SELECT dept, COUNT(*), AVG(salary) FROM emp GROUP BY dept
Every non-aggregated SELECT column must appear in GROUP BY, or the engine errors (or returns an arbitrary value in lax MySQL modes)
WHERE filters rows before grouping and cannot use aggregates; HAVING filters groups after: HAVING COUNT(*) > 5
NULL means unknown: NULL = NULL is not true, so test with IS NULL / IS NOT NULL; any comparison or arithmetic with NULL yields NULL
COUNT(*) counts all rows but COUNT(col) skips NULLs; SUM/AVG ignore NULLs; NOT IN (subquery containing NULL) returns no rows; COALESCE(x, 0) substitutes a default

chapters.title: SQL Cheat Sheet
points: DDL: CREATE TABLE t (id INT PRIMARY KEY, fk INT REFERENCES p(id) ON DELETE CASCADE); ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c TEXT; DROP TABLE t
DML: INSERT INTO t (a,b) VALUES (1,2); UPDATE t SET a=1 WHERE id=3; DELETE FROM t WHERE id=3
Query skeleton: SELECT ... FROM ... JOIN ... ON ... WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT
Joins: INNER = matches only, LEFT = all left + NULLs, FULL = all both sides, anti-join = LEFT JOIN + IS NULL
NULL rules: IS NULL not = NULL, COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col), COALESCE for defaults; always WHERE on UPDATE/DELETE
